key_insight: Standard Wasserstein DRO can overreact to rare extreme events, and adding KL regularization reduces this over-conservatism in planning.
engineering_relevance: The method helps power-system planners choose more realistic PV, wind, and storage capacities when low-probability outages or weather extremes matter.
method: Build a two-stage distributionally robust planning model for capacity expansion.
Use a Wasserstein ambiguity set augmented with a KL divergence term to limit probability inflation of rare events.
Reformulate the problem as an exponential cone program with theoretical guarantees for tractable solving.
evidence_signal: The approach was tested on PJM 5-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems, where results showed standard Wasserstein DRO becomes overly conservative under low-probability extreme events.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how the KL regularization strength is tuned, since too much or too little regularization could understate or overstate tail risk.
paper_title: On Over-Conservatism Under Low-Probability Extreme Events: A KL-Regularized Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Planning Method
